- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast peaks, especially in early/medium horizon.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase early forecast values, especially if recent history shows downward momentum.
- If model shows sharp spikes (e.g., >3x median) followed by large overshoots, apply “lag correction”: reduce forecast by 20–40% in next 3–5 days if sentiment remains neutral or negative.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of declining values), model often overreacts; dampen forecast slope in medium horizon (days 10–20).
- For horizon 1–5 days: model often underestimates if sentiment is positive; for horizon 20–30: overestimates if sentiment is negative or neutral.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or “-0.33” values, model tends to ignore sentiment and overreacts; apply “sentiment decay” rule: reduce forecast by 10–20% for each consecutive negative sentiment day.
